subject: Unexpected geo-based usage spike — request for attribution and provisional credit
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@nimblegames.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Billing Ops <billing@nimblegames.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden spike in tokens from EU region on 9/11 — please investigate

Hi Marcus / Ben,

We noticed a ~6x jump in billable token consumption from EU IP ranges starting around 2026-09-11 22:30 UTC. Our billing team flagged an unexpected charge on last night's invoice preview and asked us to escalate — attaching the CSV export from your usage portal (nimble-usage-export-20260911.csv).

Quick facts:
- Account: Nimble Games (NG-2025-0893)
- Window: 2026-09-11 22:00 UTC -> 2026-09-12 03:00 UTC
- Observed: spike concentrated on endpoints /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings

We were running an A/B feature toggle experiment for a small cohort (1.2% of traffic). There were no customer-reported incidents. Our ops team is worried this is double-counting or a routing loop from the CDN to your edge. Can you please:
1) Confirm whether requests from our primary region (us-east) could have been misattributed to EU due to a geo-tagging change on your side.
2) Provide raw request ids/sample payloads for the highest-volume minute.
3) Consider a provisional credit while you investigate — this is material for our month-end close.

Attached: nimble-usage-export-20260911.csv and a short telemetry snippet file.

Thanks,
Sam
Sr. Engineering Manager, Nimble Games

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@nimblegames.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in tokens from EU region on 9/11 — please investigate

Sam — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the exports. We're looking into it now. Quick read: usage portal shows a concentrated burst from 22:28–22:41 UTC that was routed through our EU routing tier.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Ben: I'll have you coordinate on provisional credit and commercial messaging.
- Kimberly: please prepare the provisional credit authorization form (I attached a template we use).
- Logan: can you pull request-level telemetry (request_id, route, src_ip, model, tokens_in/tokens_out) for that 13-minute window and the five highest-volume request_ids? We need raw samples for Nimble's ops team.

Sam — we'll aim to share initial telemetry samples within 4 business hours. If the spike looks like misattribution on our side we'll push a provisional credit and follow up with a formal adjustment.

Regards,
Marcus
Account Lead — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in tokens from EU region on 9/11 — telemetry and root-cause findings

Team / Sam,

I pulled the raw telemetry for NG-2025-0893 for 2026-09-11 22:15 -> 2026-09-12 03:15 UTC. Attached are the top-five request samples and a compact timeline (sample-telemetry-snippets.txt). Findings (short):

1) Source IPs: ~92% of the spike originated from a small set of IPs that resolve to Nimble's CDN edge but were geo-located to DE (Germany) due to our recent geo-IP DB update on 2026-09-11 21:50 UTC. That DB update added a new ASN mapping which incorrectly biased a block to DE.

2) Request IDs: the top 5 request_ids (listed in the attached snippets) show normal request/response patterns — no duplication within Redwood's runtime. Token counts per request are large (long prompts + system context), which explains the per-request token weight.

3) Routing: Requests were served by our EU routing tier because of the geo-IP mapping. The requests actually originated from Nimble's CDN in us-east but appear to be from DE because of the incorrect DB mapping. There is no evidence of double-billing duplicates inside our service; counts are legitimate based on tokenized payloads.

Implications: The spike is caused by geo-attribution — not double-processing. For billing, tokens were charged under EU region. Per enterprise contract NG-2025-0893 we treat regional tax/VAT based on where the request is attributed. This mapping error is on Redwood's infra change and we own the misattribution.

Recommended remediation:
- Quickly: issue a provisional regional credit for the EU VAT difference and reclassify the usage to US for billing purposes for 2026-09-11 22:28–22:41 UTC (proposed adjustment attached).
- Medium: revert or correct the geo-IP DB change and add a validation check for large-traffic customers during geo-db rollouts.

I've attached the telemetry snippets and a short CSV with affected request_ids. Let me know if you want full pcap-style logs; those are larger and we'll coordinate access.

Logan
SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@nimblegames.com>, Billing Ops <billing@nimblegames.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden spike in tokens from EU region on 9/11 — provisional credit and next steps

Hi Sam — thanks for your patience and for the quick coordination. We confirmed Logan's findings: a geo-IP DB update at 21:50 UTC caused misattribution of a subset of Nimble's CDN IPs to DE for ~13 minutes.

What we're doing now:
- Issuing a provisional billing adjustment that reclassifies the affected usage from EU to US for tax/VAT purposes and applies a credit for the EU VAT delta (see provisional-credit-form.pdf). The provisional credit amount is EUR 4,320.00 (we'll convert on the final invoice per your preference).
- Our finance team will produce a corrected invoice and a short explanatory memo. Kimberly will send the formal credit note and the corrected invoice within 3 business days.
- Engineering: we've reverted the geo-IP DB change and added a guardrail preventing geo-db rollouts during active high-volume windows for customers marked as 'sensitive'.

Sam, please confirm you accept the provisional credit approach. If you'd prefer a different resolution (full refund, token-level adjustment, or a systems-level post-mortem), we can align on the next steps.

Appreciate you flagging this — we'll follow up with the formal docs.

Best,
Ben
Enterprise Success, Redwood Inference

Attachment references: provisional-credit-form.pdf (signed copy to follow); nimble-usage-export-20260911.csv; sample-telemetry-snippets.txt
